summary: For money cases, each side chooses a judge and a third judge is added. The mishnah also teaches when one side can turn down the other side's judge or witnesses.

chunks.en: Money cases are judged by three.
chunks.st: Cases of monetary law are adjudicated by three. They are chosen in the following manner:

chunks.en: This one chooses one judge for himself,
chunks.st: This litigant chooses one for himself

chunks.en: and that one chooses one judge for himself,
chunks.st: and that litigant chooses one for himself,

chunks.en: and the two of them choose one more.
chunks.st: and the two of them choose one more for themselves;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי דַיָּנִין בּוֹרְרִין לָהֶן עוֹד אֶחָד.
chunks.en: the two judges choose one more.
chunks.st: The two judges that were chosen choose one more judge for themselves.

chunks.en: This one can turn down that one's judge,
chunks.st: This litigant can disqualify the judge chosen by that litigant

chunks.en: and that one can turn down this one's judge.
chunks.st: and that litigant can disqualify the judge chosen by this litigant;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: when is that? When he brings proof about them
chunks.st: When can one of the litigants disqualify the judges? Only when he brings evidence about them

chunks.en: that they are relatives or not fit to judge.
chunks.st: that they are related to one of the litigants or to each other, or that they are disqualified from serving as judges for another reason.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיוּ כְשֵׁרִים אוֹ מֻמְחִין,
chunks.en: But if they are fit judges, or experts,
chunks.st: But if they are fit to serve as judges or are experts ordained by the court,

chunks.en: he cannot turn them down.
chunks.st: he cannot disqualify them.

chunks.en: This one can turn down that one's witnesses,
chunks.st: This litigant can disqualify the witnesses of that litigant

chunks.en: and that one can turn down this one's witnesses.
chunks.st: and that litigant can disqualify the witnesses of this litigant;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא מֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶם רְאָיָה
chunks.en: when is that? When he brings proof about them
chunks.st: When can one litigant disqualify the other’s witnesses? Only when he brings evidence about them

chunks.en: that they are relatives or not fit to be witnesses.
chunks.st: that they are related to one of the litigants or to each other, or that they are disqualified from bearing witness for another reason.

chunks.en: But if they are fit,
chunks.st: But if they are fit to serve as witnesses,

chunks.en: he cannot turn them down.
chunks.st: he cannot disqualify them.

summary: What if a person agrees to let someone who is not a proper judge decide his case, or agrees to let the other side make a promise instead of a real shevuah? Can he change his mind?

chunks.en: If one said to the other, "I trust my father to judge my case,"
chunks.st: If one litigant says to the other: My father is trusted to adjudicate for me, or:

chunks.en: or "I trust your father,"
chunks.st: Your father is trusted to adjudicate for me, or:

chunks.en: or "I trust three cowherds,"
chunks.explain: People who do not know the halachos well.
chunks.st: Three cattle herders, who are not proficient in halakha, are trusted to adjudicate for me,
chunks.stMore: all of whom are disqualified from serving as judges,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he can change his mind.
chunks.st: The one who made the offer can retract it,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he cannot change his mind.
chunks.st: He cannot retract it, but must accept their verdict.

chunks.en: If he had to swear a shevuah to his friend,
chunks.st: Similarly, one who was obligated by Torah law to take an oath to another, which is done while grasping a sacred object,

words.note: A very serious promise made holding a holy object.

chunks.he: וְאָמַר לוֹ דּוֹר לִי בְחַיֵּי רֹאשְׁךָ,
chunks.en: and his friend said to him, "Just make a promise to me on the life of your head,"
chunks.st: and the latter said to him: Instead of taking an oath, merely vow to me by the life of your head that what you claim is true,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he can change his mind.
chunks.st: The one who made the offer can retract it,
chunks.stMore: and demand that the other litigant take an oath, as he is obligated to do by Torah law.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he cannot change his mind.
chunks.st: He cannot retract
chunks.stMore: his offer. Once he has agreed to accept a vow, which is of less severity than an oath, he cannot retract his agreement.

summary: Some people may not be witnesses because they make money in dishonest ways, like gamblers and people who lend with interest. Rabbi Yehudah says this is only when it is their only job.

chunks.en: These are the people who are not fit to be witnesses:
chunks.st: And these on the following list are the ones who are disqualified
chunks.stMore: by the Sages from bearing witness due to their unseemly behavior, as they are considered wicked individuals guilty of monetary transgressions:

chunks.en: one who plays with dice for money,
chunks.st: One who plays with dice [bekubbiyya] for money,

chunks.en: and one who lends with interest,
chunks.st: and one who lends money with interest,

words.note: Ribbis: extra money the Torah forbids taking for a loan.

chunks.en: and those who race pigeons,
chunks.st: and those who fly pigeons,

words.note: They bet money on which bird wins.

chunks.en: and those who sell Shemittah fruit.
chunks.st: and merchants who trade in the produce of the Sabbatical
chunks.stMore: Year, which may be eaten but may not be sold as an object of commerce.

words.note: Fruit of the seventh year may not be bought and sold for business.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.he: בִּתְחִלָּה הָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתָן אוֹסְפֵי שְׁבִיעִית,
chunks.en: At first they called them "gatherers of Shemittah fruit."
chunks.st: Initially, people would call them: Gatherers of the produce of the Sabbatical Year.

chunks.en: Once the tax collectors became many,
chunks.st: Once the tax collectors grew abundant

chunks.en: they went back to calling them "traders of Shemittah fruit."
chunks.st: they would then call them: Merchants who trade in the produce of the Sabbatical Year, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֻמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הִיא,
chunks.en: When is this? When they have no other job but this.
chunks.st: When are the people listed above disqualified from bearing witness? It is when they have no occupation but this one.

chunks.he: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהֶן אֻמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הִיא, כְּשֵׁרִין:
chunks.en: But if they have another job, they are fit.
chunks.st: But if they have an occupation other than this one, although they also make money by these inappropriate means, they are fit to bear witness.

summary: Relatives may not be witnesses or judges for each other. The mishnah lists which relatives, and teaches what happens if someone stops being a relative.

chunks.en: These are the relatives:
chunks.st: And these are the ones disqualified from bearing witness or from serving as judges due to their status as relatives of one of the litigants or of each other:

chunks.he: אָבִיו וְאָחִיו וַאֲחִי אָבִיו וַאֲחִי אִמּוֹ
chunks.en: his father, his brother, his father's brother, his mother's brother,
chunks.st: One’s father, brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle,

chunks.en: his sister's husband, his father's sister's husband,
chunks.st: and his sister’s husband, and the husband of his paternal aunt,

chunks.en: his mother's sister's husband,
chunks.st: and the husband of his maternal aunt,

chunks.en: his mother's husband, his father-in-law, and his brother-in-law,
chunks.st: and his mother’s husband, and his father-in-law, and his brother-in-law, i.e., the husband of his wife’s sister.

chunks.en: they, and their sons, and their sons-in-law,
chunks.st: They themselves, all of these people, and also their sons, and their sons-in-law are considered relatives.

chunks.en: and his stepson only.
chunks.st: And his stepson alone
chunks.stMore: is disqualified, but not his stepson’s sons or sons-in-law.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: this is the mishnah of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: This aforementioned halakha is Rabbi Akiva’s version of the mishna.

chunks.en: But the first mishnah said:
chunks.st: But the initial version of the mishna reads as follows:

chunks.en: His uncle and his uncle's son,
chunks.st: His uncle and the son of his uncle,

chunks.en: and anyone who could inherit from him,
chunks.st: and anyone who is fit to inherit from him.
chunks.stMore: Only paternal relatives, who are fit to inherit from him, are disqualified; maternal relatives, who do not inherit from him, are not disqualified from bearing witness about him or from adjudicating his case.

chunks.en: and anyone who is related to him at that time.
chunks.st: And the halakha disqualifying a relative from bearing witness or serving as a judge is referring to anyone who is related to him at the time of the trial.

chunks.en: If he was a relative and then stopped being related,
chunks.st: If one was once a relative and became unrelated
chunks.stMore: by the time of the trial, e.g., he married the daughter of one of the litigants, but she died or they were divorced,

chunks.en: he is fit.
chunks.st: in this case he is fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even if his daughter passed away,
chunks.st: Even if his daughter died

chunks.en: but he has children from her,
chunks.st: but her husband, the former son-in-law, has children from her,

chunks.en: he is still a relative.
chunks.st: he is still considered a relative; the children cause them to remain related.

summary: A close friend or an enemy of one side may not be a witness or a judge. The Sages say Jews are not suspected of lying for that reason.

chunks.en: The one who loves and the one who hates.
chunks.st: One who loves or one who hates one of the litigants is also disqualified.

chunks.en: "The one who loves" is his best man at his wedding.
chunks.st: With regard to one who loves one of the litigants, this is referring to his groomsman.

chunks.en: "The one who hates" is anyone who did not speak with him
chunks.st: One who hates is referring to anyone who, out of enmity, did not speak with the litigant for

chunks.en: for three days because he was angry at him.
chunks.st: three days.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.en: Jews are not suspected of that.
chunks.st: The Jewish people are not suspected of bearing false witness due to love or hate.

summary: The judges check the witnesses one at a time to make sure they tell the truth. Then the judges discuss the case and decide by a majority.

chunks.en: How do they check the witnesses?
chunks.st: How do the judges examine the witnesses?

chunks.en: They bring them in and warn them to tell the truth.
chunks.st: They bring them into a room in the courthouse and intimidate them so that they will speak only the truth.

chunks.en: They send everyone else outside,
chunks.st: And they take all the people, other than the judges, outside
chunks.stMore: so that they should not tell the other witnesses the questions the judges ask and the answers the first witness gives,

chunks.en: and they leave only the oldest of them.
chunks.st: and they leave only the eldest of the witnesses to testify first.

chunks.en: And they say to him, "Tell us,
chunks.st: And they say to him: Say

chunks.he: הֵיאַךְ אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁזֶּה חַיָּב לָזֶה.
chunks.en: how do you know that this one owes money to that one?"
chunks.st: how exactly you know that this litigant owes money to that litigant, as the plaintiff claims.

chunks.en: If he said,
chunks.st: If he said:

chunks.he: הוּא אָמַר לִי שֶׁאֲנִי חַיָּב לוֹ,
chunks.en: "He told me that he owes him,"
chunks.st: The defendant said to me: It is true that I owe the plaintiff, or if he says:

chunks.he: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי אָמַר לִי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב לוֹ,
chunks.en: or "A certain man told me that he owes him,"
chunks.st: So-and-so said to me that the defendant owes the plaintiff,

chunks.en: he has said nothing.
chunks.st: the witness has said nothing and his testimony is disregarded.

chunks.en: It does not count until he says,
chunks.st: It is not valid testimony unless he says:

chunks.en: "In front of us he admitted
chunks.st: The defendant admitted in our presence to the plaintiff

chunks.en: that he owes him two hundred zuz."
chunks.st: that he owes him, e.g., two hundred dinars.
chunks.stMore: By admitting to the debt in the presence of witnesses he renders himself liable to pay the amount that he mentioned.

chunks.en: Afterward they bring in the second witness
chunks.st: And afterward they bring in the second witness

chunks.en: and check him.
chunks.st: and examine him in the same manner.

chunks.en: If what they say matches,
chunks.st: If their statements are found to be congruent

chunks.en: the judges discuss the case.
chunks.explain: They talk it over and give reasons.
chunks.st: the judges then discuss the matter.

chunks.en: If two judges say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: If the opinions of the judges are divided, as two judges say that the defendant is exempt from payment

chunks.en: and one says "guilty," he is not guilty.
chunks.st: and one says he is liable to pay, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If two say "guilty,"
chunks.st: If two say he is liable

chunks.en: and one says "not guilty," he is guilty.
chunks.st: and one says he is exempt, he is liable.

chunks.en: If one says "not guilty,"
chunks.st: If one says he is liable

chunks.en: and one says "guilty,"
chunks.st: and one says he is exempt,

chunks.en: or even if two say "not guilty"
chunks.st: or even if two of the judges deem him exempt

chunks.en: or two say "guilty,"
chunks.st: or two of them deem him liable,

chunks.en: and one says "I do not know,"
chunks.st: and the other one says: I do not know,

chunks.en: they must add more judges.
chunks.st: the court must add more judges
chunks.stMore: and then rule in accordance with the majority opinion. This is because the one who abstains is considered as though he is not a member of the court.

summary: When the judges finish, the head judge tells each side the decision. A judge may not tell anyone afterward that he disagreed with the others, because that is like tale-bearing.

chunks.en: When they finished deciding the case,
chunks.st: After the judges finish the matter and reach a decision,

chunks.en: they would bring the two sides in.
chunks.st: they bring in the litigants.

chunks.en: The biggest of the judges says,
chunks.st: The greatest of the judges says:

chunks.en: "So-and-so, you are not guilty,"
chunks.st: So-and-so, you are exempt from paying; or:

chunks.en: or "So-and-so, you are guilty."
chunks.st: So-and-so, you are liable to pay.

chunks.en: And how do we know that when one of the judges goes out
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that when the judge leaves the courtroom

chunks.en: he may not say, "I said not guilty,
chunks.st: he may not say: I deemed you exempt

chunks.en: and my friends said guilty,
chunks.st: and my colleagues deemed you liable,

chunks.he: אֲבָל מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה שֶׁחֲבֵרַי רַבּוּ עָלָי,
chunks.en: but what can I do, my friends were more than me"?
chunks.st: but what can I do, as my colleagues outnumbered me and consequently you were deemed liable?

chunks.en: About this it says,
chunks.st: About this it is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not go around as a tale-bearer among your people,"
chunks.st: “You shall not go as a talebearer among your people” (Leviticus 19:16),

chunks.he: וְאוֹמֵר הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל מְגַלֶּה סּוֹד (משלי יא):
chunks.en: and it says, "One who goes around as a tale-bearer tells secrets."
chunks.st: and it says: “One who goes about as a talebearer reveals secrets,
chunks.stMore: but one who is of a faithful spirit conceals a matter” (Proverbs 11:13).

summary: If someone finds new proof after his case was decided, can he change the ruling? The Sages and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel argue about proof found late, but all agree that hidden proof brought at the last moment is worthless.

chunks.en: As long as he brings proof,
chunks.st: Any time one of the litigants brings additional proof,

chunks.en: he can undo the ruling.
chunks.st: he can overturn the verdict
chunks.stMore: that was decided according to previous proofs.

chunks.en: If they said to him,
chunks.st: If one litigant said to the other:

chunks.en: "Bring all the proof you have
chunks.st: Bring all the proofs that you have

chunks.en: from now until thirty days,"
chunks.st: from now until thirty days from now,

chunks.en: if he found it within thirty days, he can undo the ruling.
chunks.st: if he found additional proof within thirty days, he can overturn the verdict.

chunks.en: After thirty days, he cannot undo it.
chunks.st: If he found it after thirty days, he cannot overturn the verdict anymore.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: "What can this person do,
chunks.st: He can still overturn the verdict, as what should this litigant,

chunks.en: who did not find it within thirty days,
chunks.st: who sought and did not find additional proof within thirty days

chunks.en: and found it after thirty?"
chunks.explain: So he can still undo the ruling.
chunks.st: but found it after thirty days, have done?

chunks.en: If they said to him, "Bring witnesses,"
chunks.st: In a case where one litigant said to the other: Bring witnesses,

chunks.en: and he said, "I have no witnesses,"
chunks.st: and the latter said: I have no witnesses,

chunks.en: and they said, "Bring proof,"
chunks.st: and the former said to him: Bring a proof,

chunks.en: and he said, "I have no proof,"
chunks.st: and he said: I have no proof,

chunks.he: וּלְאַחַר זְמָן הֵבִיא רְאָיָה וּמָצָא עֵדִים,
chunks.en: and later he brought proof or found witnesses,
chunks.st: and he later brought a proof or found witnesses,

chunks.en: it is worth nothing.
chunks.st: in this case, this proof or these witnesses are worth nothing.
chunks.stMore: It is apparently a false proof or false testimony.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: "What can this person do,
chunks.st: What should this litigant,

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ עֵדִים
chunks.en: who did not know that he had witnesses,
chunks.st: who did not know that he has witnesses

chunks.en: and then found witnesses,
chunks.st: and ultimately found witnesses,

chunks.he: לֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ רְאָיָה
chunks.en: or did not know that he had proof,
chunks.st: or who did not know that he has a proof

chunks.en: and then found proof?"
chunks.st: and ultimately found proof, have done? Therefore, he can still overturn the verdict.

chunks.en: If they said to him, "Bring witnesses,"
chunks.st: If at the beginning of the discussion in the court

chunks.he: אָמַר אֵין לִי עֵדִים, הָבֵא רְאָיָה
chunks.en: and he said, "I have no witnesses"; "Bring proof,"
chunks.st: one did not bring witnesses

chunks.en: and he said, "I have no proof,"
chunks.st: or other evidence for his claims,

chunks.en: and then he saw he was about to lose the case,
chunks.st: but then he saw that he was about to be deemed liable to pay in the judgment,

chunks.en: and he said, "Bring over so-and-so and so-and-so to be my witnesses,"
chunks.st: and said: Bring so-and-so and so-and-so, and they will testify on my behalf,

words.en: and let them testify for me

chunks.en: or he took out proof from his belt,
chunks.st: or he pulled out a proof from under his belt [pundato],

chunks.en: it is worth nothing.
chunks.explain: If it were true, he would not have hidden it until now.
chunks.st: even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that this is worth nothing.
chunks.stMore: If there was truth in the testimony of these witnesses or in this proof, he would not have hidden it until now.
